technical_notes: SLO framing proposal discussed: separate SLOs for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints.

Non-streaming (batched generate): define latency as server egress time (LB->response complete) and report p50/p95/p99 over 5-min windows; target: p50<50ms, p95<200ms, p99<450ms for 2K concurrent connections typical workload.
Streaming endpoints: split metrics into TTF (time-to-first-token) and time-to-last-token (TTLT). Proposed targets: TTF p95<120ms, TTLT p95 tied to token-rate (e.g., 20 tokens at 50ms/token).

Client-side vs server-side: propose canonical measurement = client SDK end-to-end (request sent -> first token emitted / final token) for product SLAs, and server-side instrumented metrics (ingress->egress) for ops/debugging. Both must be published with mapping table.
Clock sync & attribution: will use TLS-record timestamps + monotonic clocks in SDK; where possible, use server-generated event IDs to correlate. Agree on +/- skew tolerance of 50ms for client clocks.
Percentile calculation: sliding-window, weighted by request count, 95th/99th computed over 1h rolling windows with hourly summaries; provide raw histograms for forensic review.
Cold vs warm starts: cold-start latencies excluded from SLO baseline for first 30s after node spin-up; quantify cold-start rate in infra report.

Batching and KV-cache hits: SLOs assume warm KV cache hit-rate >= 85% and batching scheme configured as per Redwood optimize recommendations; if hit-rate < threshold, SLOs re-baselined or compensated financially.
Error handling: retries counted separately; SLOs apply to successful responses. Retries/backoff behavior to be documented in runbook.
Sampling and observability: full tracing for 0.5% of requests, histogram retention 90 days (ops), aggregated 13 months (legal/audit).
